0038e900fc5f97c1.text: The alderman’s offer. [short pause] Hodd sends for you after dark. He has a bottle open and the shutters closed. He is a practical man. He has done the arithmetic: a witch hunter who leaves happy is cheaper than a witch hunter who leaves angry. [short pause] "I don’t care about the girl," he says. "I care about the town. Give him something. Give him the girl, give him the old woman in Ashbrook, give him a stranger off the road. He goes home, we go back to work." [short pause] He does not like you much. He thinks you make things complicated. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: "Give him nothing. He leaves with an empty cage or he leaves with a problem." [short pause] Two: Take Hodd’s side. The town first. Point Rook at a stranger on the road.

Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

[short pause] Four elves are in the Mahakam hills, alive, because of you. They told you to light a fire on the north tower when the horns come. [short pause] Nilfgaard knows the bridge is held by a troll and nothing else. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

Then the thing itself, in a clearing, crows pouring out of it. You unmake it with the forest watching, and it takes everything you have. [short pause] When it dies, the mark passes. You feel it settle behind your sternum like a swallowed coal. Something in the wood will remember you. [short pause] Aldo pays. Ysolde lives. The forest is quiet, and angry.

02932e84aad30500.text: Aurelio. [short pause] He comes up out of the well like smoke that forgot it was supposed to rise. Black coat, open throat, a face that is still mostly a face. He speaks Nilfgaardian, then Common, then just sound. He is asking which way is south. He is asking for his mother. [short pause] You never went down. You do not know his name, and he can tell. [short pause] He feels you before he sees you. Wraiths and sorceresses recognize each other. Neither likes it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Fight. End it clean. [short pause] Two: Lay him to rest. (You need his name, his letter, and someone who can say it: Marga unshaken, or Lukas willing.) [short pause] Three: Glamour. Show him the river and call it the road home.

02f6beb79fac4c91.text: Light a fire on the north tower first. The elves said they would see it. [short pause] Berna’s whole stock of lamp oil goes up on the tower in one minute. Across the river, in the hills, nothing. Then one light. Then six. [short pause] You run for the bridge.

03deade7a866024e.text: Old wood, closed. [short pause] The north wood tonight: [short pause] The leshen is waiting for white cloaks. [short pause] A forest remembers who kept faith with it, and who did not.

Get it wrong, Bogdan is sad." He sits down, which takes a while. [short pause] "What has a bed but never sleeps, a mouth but never eats, and runs but never walks?" [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: A river. [short pause] Two: A troll. [short pause] Three: Skip the game. Show me what is under the bridge.

04e92dc77f3da676.text: Bogdan. [short pause] Bogdan is nine feet of river rock with moss for eyebrows and a toll-collector’s satchel that used to be a Redanian saddlebag. He stands in the middle of the bridge with his arms folded and says: "Toll. Cheese or story. No story about a dog. Bogdan has heard every dog story." [short pause] He looks at you the way a very large child looks at a very fancy cake. "Pretty lady is a story herself," he says, which is the nicest thing anyone has said to you in Greyhollow. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Pay in a story. Tell him something true about yourself. [short pause] Two: Pay in a story. Make one up. [short pause] Three: Fight. The council wants a bridge. [short pause] Four: Threaten him. Let him see what you are.

0502ee2539daf59d.text: The boy. [short pause] Lukas is at the well at dawn, where you left him, grey-faced, waiting to find out what you are going to do. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [short pause] Berthold’s eighty crowns are in your coat. [short pause] Ida is in the crowd with Tam on her hip. She is watching you, not Lukas. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope. [short pause] Four: Blame the drowner. Take the money. Leave.

[short pause] In front of the bakery, a twelve-year-old girl is standing very still with her hands folded. A Nilfgaardian captain, or what is left of one, is on the cobbles in front of her. She lit one candle, and only one, and it was him. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. Rook. He has a warrant and a column and nothing left to be ashamed of. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Face the Order here. Say the thing out loud: nobody sent them. [short pause] Two: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Three: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

Greyhollow is an island now, and Jens the ferryman is the richest man in it.

[short pause] Something in you is different on the walk out. The Fire’s eye on you grows.

[short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

0e19ba54442f59da.text: The search. [short pause] Four of Rook’s men come through the inn at dusk with torches and a dog. They are not subtle. They turn over the beds, they open the flour barrels, they put a boot through Berna’s cellar door. [short pause] Liesl is in the back room, sitting at the table with her hands folded, three candles in front of her, none of them lit. A man asks her name. She tells him. A man asks if she is afraid. "No," she says, and nothing on the table moves. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Stand behind her and say nothing. [short pause] Two: Get her out the back before they reach the room. Do not make her test it.

0e25382294cd04a5.text: Pay in a story. Make one up. [short pause] You tell him about a dragon that fell in love with a lighthouse. He loves it. He does not know it is nonsense. [short pause] He says you can cross, and asks if you want to see what is under the bridge.

0e28c4fcbbed7836.text: Talk to Berthold. [short pause] He is waiting with a drink and a very steady smile.

0e2b614fc0b83a71.text: Liesl. [short pause] Liesl is small for twelve and will not look up. When Matthis says the word "hunters" the candle on the table goes from a flame to a torch and back. He flinches. She flinches harder. [short pause] You have seen this before. A Source: someone born with magic that leaks out before anyone teaches them to hold it. In the old days a child like this got sent to a magic school, Aretuza for girls, Ban Ard for boys. In Redania now, she gets a cage. [short pause] Liesl finally looks up. "Am I a monster?" she asks you. Not her father. You. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: "No. You are a girl who can do something most people cannot. That is all." [short pause] Two: "I am a monster, by most people’s reckoning. So is half of what I hunt. The word does not mean much." [short pause] Three: "The Fire thinks so. That is the only opinion that matters for the next three days."

0e30adbde762f907.text: Axii the man at the hearth. He has seen nothing. [short pause] He blinks, nods, and walks out. The dog does not nod. The dog keeps looking up, and one of the other men notices the dog. [short pause] It holds. Barely. Someone will mention the dog to Rook.

[short pause] Two: Lay him to rest. Give him his name, burn the knife, let the boy say it. [short pause] Three: Glamour. Show him the river and call it the road home. [short pause] Four: Let him have Lukas. The boy is standing right there.

0f9679793b00ffc4.text: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope. [short pause] Berthold argues. Orm the miller does not. Lukas walks out of the north gate with his bow, a loaf, and the eleven florens, if you gave them back. [short pause] He will end up in someone’s army. Everyone does.

100e559459c327a0.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Look at the well. [short pause] Two: Talk to Berthold. [short pause] Three: Wait for nightfall at the well.

10908f9e76c5aa52.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] At the head of the column, under the black banner, a captain reins in and shouts a name across the bridge. "Aurelio." Then: "Who wrote to Vicovaro?" [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Answer the captain. "I did. He was laid to rest. His mother knows." [short pause] Two: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Three: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

10c343e9d4f69f11.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] Liesl is in the chimney with Pip. Liesl was in the chimney for all of it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

10e9825b5b953834.text: The narrow part. [short pause] It holds for an hour. Then the right-hand parapet goes and they are over it in a wave, and you are backing up the bridge one yard at a time. [short pause] Quen is gone. Your sword arm is somebody else’s. There is a thing you could do here that witchers are told not to do: drink everything in the bag at once and see what is left of you after. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Drink everything. Let the mutations have the night. [short pause] Two: Hold with what you have. No more than that.

115cf424cd8c90ae.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

1183dab9c0a4bc61.text: The widow. [short pause] You find Marga tied to the shrine post in the square with a split lip and a crowd of six deciding what comes next. The rope is over the beam already. [short pause] The miller, a wide man named Orm, has the end of it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Talk Orm down. "Hang her and the well is still poisoned tomorrow." [short pause] Two: Cut the rope. Let them look at you and think.

[short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is mending. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

11f3a008e84c8f98.text: The leshen. [short pause] It comes at midnight, after the rite, because you are at the treeline alone and it has been curious since the road. Antlers like a fallen tree. A body that is bark and shadow and crows. It does not have a face. It has a place where a face would be, and the place looks at you. [short pause] It speaks to you as an equal, because tonight you are. Old power recognizes old power. It asks, without words, what you want. [short pause] It knows you burned the totem. It is not angry. It is interested, the way a cat is interested in a mouse that bit it. [short pause] It tells you the terms, which have not changed in a thousand years. One life, freely marked, and the wood keeps the peace. The oak was cut. The price went up. Three woodcutters were the interest. Ysolde is the principal. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Ask it to take the debt out of the guild instead. They cut the oak. [short pause] Two: Ask it what it fears. [short pause] Three: Say nothing. Let it finish, and decide.

Aldo, foreman of the woodcutters’ guild, will pay a hundred and twenty crowns for the leshen in the north wood: three men dead, the rest refusing to go in. A leshen is an ancient forest spirit, antlered and tree-tall, that commands the wolves and crows and treats the wood as its own. Elder Hesper of Thornwick, the village at the wood’s edge that still keeps the old gods, will pay nothing and asks you, please, to leave the forest its master. [short pause] The leshen has marked someone. Thornwick will not say who. The woodcutters do not care who. [short pause] You can feel it from the road. Something old, and awake, and interested in you specifically. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take Aldo’s coin and go in. [short pause] Two: Go in for Thornwick. See what the forest wants.

[short pause] Nilfgaard thinks there are crossbows on the towers. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

1ba540151ac152ed.text: Hold with what you have. No more than that. [short pause] You do not need the other thing. By dawn the column is backing down the south road and the bridge is still a bridge.

1baff65a505fcfde.text: Long shadows. [short pause] Horns on the south road. A Nilfgaardian raiding column, two hundred soldiers of the southern empire, come to burn a river town for the lesson it teaches other river towns. They need the bridge to cross the Pontar. Everyone in Greyhollow needs it more. [short pause] Rook is with them, at the back, with a face that has been waiting for this. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: Pip: "Bridge first. Everything else is after." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The bridge. Now.

He stands there blinking. His two men saw your hand glow. The Fire’s eye on you is wide open now. [short pause] His men do not need the name. They have the bakery.

46f20feb73bf97d2.text: Questions. [short pause] Dren the clerk is in the cage, white as his own candles. Father Ansel is standing beside it with his hands folded, saying nothing, which is the bravest thing he can manage. [short pause] Rook asks to speak with you anyway. Alone, he says, and then brings two men. He is polite. He knows what you are. He asks where the baker’s girl is, and then, before you answer, he asks about Ashbrook, and the bridge, and a light some people saw. [short pause] He is building a case. Not against the girl. Against you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. The bakery is three doors from the inn. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Lie. Smoothly. The girl ran off to Oxenfurt a week ago. [short pause] Two: Bribe him. Fifty crowns for a letter that says Greyhollow is clean. [short pause] Three: Let him see your eyes. Remind him what a witcher does to men who threaten him. [short pause] Four: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here?

46fcc20a3b9982c0.text: "I work alone." [short pause] Pip nods seriously, waits until you turn around, and climbs into your coat pocket anyway. [short pause] Berna, still not looking up: "He does this."

46fdba66af62b856.text: Skip the game. Show me what is under the bridge. [short pause] "No game, no secret." He shrugs, which is a geological event, and leads you down.

4729fae034fd4372.text: The boy. [short pause] The whole village is in the square at dawn, because Berthold’s son confessed in his father’s kitchen last night and the maid heard it through the floor. Lukas is standing by the well with his hands at his sides. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [short pause] Berthold’s eighty crowns are in your coat. [short pause] Ida is in the crowd with Tam on her hip. She is watching you, not Lukas. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope. [short pause] Four: Blame the drowner. Take the money. Leave.

475dbe5dd23e2bb3.text: Take the letter and the knife. [short pause] Both go in your coat. The letter smells of river. His mother’s name is Livia.

477a24127ab75fd5.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

477e88a9700c6d80.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] A letter is going south to a woman named Livia. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

47acb62ac2ed58ae.text: The price. [short pause] Aldo wants it dead. Thornwick wants it fed. Ysolde wants to be sixteen. The leshen wants what it has always wanted, and will take it from someone. [short pause] There is no clean door. Pick one. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Kill Ysolde. Then the leshen. It is the only clean way. [short pause] Two: Burn the totems and fight it with the mark intact. Take the mark on yourself. [short pause] Three: Give it Aldo. He cut the oak. [short pause] Four: Bargain with it. Offer it better prey than a village girl: the ones in white, when they come back. [short pause] Five: Walk away. Tell Aldo the forest is not lumber.

47fcc33fe297379b.text: Face the Order here. Say the thing out loud: nobody sent them. [short pause] You say it to the square: Rook came on a clerk’s letter. No order from Oxenfurt. No warrant but his own hand. Thirty men who thought they were the Church look at a captain who is, legally, a man with a grudge. [short pause] Half of them lower their torches. The other half look at Rook. Rook looks at the bridge, and then at the road.

481aa35ca005251e.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] You have a name and a knife that match. Lukas. L. B. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Talk to Berthold. [short pause] Two: Go up to the hunting blind. Find Lukas before dark. [short pause] Three: Wait for nightfall at the well.

49a547984a28f074.text: The square. [short pause] Greyhollow is burning. The inn, the chapel, the mill. There are Nilfgaardians in the square and they are not in a hurry. [short pause] Liesl is in Ashbrook with Marga. Nothing came near Ashbrook. A charm on a lintel, maybe. Marga is not saying. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

49fc0b3e54455f4c.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is on the bridge, but he does not know you, and he does not know whose side you are on. He fights the first thing that reaches him. It is a Nilfgaardian, which is luck, not loyalty. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

4a1f6fc653da3cdc.text: Let him go. [short pause] He goes. For now. Your name goes with him.

4a96f51adc1eba6b.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran from the bridge into the north wood did not come out of the north wood. The bargain was: the guild leaves, the wood keeps the peace. Two hundred men with torches are not the peace. Thornwick heard it from the fields: the whole wood, breathing in. [short pause] On the south bank, forty men under a captain named for a dead man’s brother never crossed. He will be court-martialed in Vicovaro. He knew that when he did it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

4ae3b94927a73abf.text: What he was guarding. [short pause] You find the camp while looking for his hoard. There is no hoard. There are four elves on a ledge above the water, a mother, a grandfather, two children, and a half-wheel of very good cheese. [short pause] "He said no one would come," the mother says. "He said he was the toll." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Help them cross north tonight. [short pause] Two: Tell Hodd. Collect the second bounty. [short pause] Three: Leave them. Not your contract.

4b0b0e052151b60f.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She can lie with a straight face now. Rook has her mother’s name in his book. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

4b0dbcef8998c478.text: Say the word. [short pause] The glamour goes first, then the sky. For the length of one word there is no night over the Pontar, only you. [short pause] It is enough. The column breaks. You come down off the bridge as yourself, which is the last time anyone in Velen will see that face without knowing what it is. The Fire’s eye is a sun now.

4b6f95b4d9501271.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan is a pile of rock at the foot of the arch. Carts roll over him. [short pause] Four elves are in the Mahakam hills, alive, because of you. They told you to light a fire on the north tower when the horns come. [short pause] Nilfgaard knows the bridge is held by a troll and nothing else. [short pause] Someone paid the Redanian garrison to leave. You do not know who yet. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

4b89bdd22b714fe7.text: The knock. [short pause] They come at midnight. Rook and all six, torches, the cage on wheels, a warrant he wrote himself. Someone told him where you sleep. Pip says the alderman did, and Pip is usually right about who smells of guilt. [short pause] They are not here for Liesl first. They are here for you. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Fight through them. [short pause] Two: Run. Out the back, into the dark. [short pause] Three: Walk out the front door and make him explain, to the whole street, why six armed men need a cage for a baker’s child.

4ba4ee6497668105.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She can light one candle without lighting the others. She stared down the Fire at her own kitchen table. She looks at you like you hung the moon. [short pause] Dren the clerk went to Oxenfurt in her place. The Fire ate its own, and Father Ansel has not slept since. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

4bcb2ea2c6e0e5af.text: The narrow part. [short pause] It does not hold. It was never going to. You are off the bridge in ten minutes with what is left of whoever came, and the town is lit behind you. [short pause] Quen is gone. Your sword arm is somebody else’s. There is a thing you could do here that witchers are told not to do: drink everything in the bag at once and see what is left of you after. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Drink everything. Let the mutations have the night. [short pause] Two: Hold with what you have. No more than that.

4c336a21d5f04a11.text: Walk out the front door and make him explain, to the whole street, why six armed men need a cage for a baker’s child. [short pause] It works because the town is already outside, holding lanterns, and because Rook, for all his sermons, has never once been asked a question by a crowd. [short pause] Berna opens the cage herself. Rook leaves at dawn with it empty and a face like a slapped priest. [short pause] Liesl climbs down from the chimney covered in soot and bows. The town laughs. Rook hears it from the road. [short pause] He will not forget this. Trust rises.

4c56aba3784789a7.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan is a pile of rock at the foot of the arch. Carts roll over him. [short pause] Four elves are somewhere. You did not ask. [short pause] Nilfgaard knows the bridge is held by a troll and nothing else. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

4c588e6ec9f49bd5.text: Burn it. The dead do not need mail. [short pause] It goes up in a second. Pip says nothing, which for Pip is a speech.

4ca40e5b45850f49.text: Sit down. Ask the grandfather where they are going. [short pause] He speaks slowly, in a Common that is older than yours. Mahakam, the dwarf mountains to the east. There are elves in the high valleys there that the kingdoms have not bothered to hunt yet. His son died getting them this far. [short pause] He says: "The troll is kinder than any man we have met since the Pontar." He is not trying to make you feel anything. It works anyway.

4d6a1879eb2dbbf6.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Ashbrook with Marga and the chickens, learning things nobody writes down. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

4d6f95e5007b5b84.text: The quest board. [short pause] The story is told. Pip says you can read the ledger again, or start over and see what the other one would have done. [long pause] One: Salt in the Well. [short pause] Two: The Toll. [short pause] Three: The Spark. [short pause] Four: Old Wood. [short pause] Five: Long Shadows.

4e0d049c1ba9173f.text: "I am a monster, by most people’s reckoning. So is half of what I hunt. The word does not mean much." [short pause] She looks at your eyes for a long time. "They’re yellow." "Yes." "Do people run?" "Some." She thinks about that and seems, oddly, comforted.

4e3a74938226eb1a.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas hangs from the mill. His father will not speak your name. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

4e895ffa4af264df.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

4ef8a460ee2b95ef.text: Long shadows. [short pause] Horns on the south road. A Nilfgaardian raiding column, two hundred soldiers of the southern empire, come to burn a river town for the lesson it teaches other river towns. They need the bridge to cross the Pontar. Everyone in Greyhollow needs it more. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: Pip: "Bridge first. Everything else is after." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Light a fire on the north tower first. The elves said they would see it. [short pause] Two: The bridge. Now.

4f55cb638a0ce0dd.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] L. B. Half the men in Ashbrook have a B in their name. Only one of them has a father with glass windows. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Talk to Marga. [short pause] Two: Go up to the hunting blind. Find Lukas before dark. [short pause] Three: Wait for nightfall at the well.

4feddfb4401f0773.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] Liesl kept her face dull and her story boring and walked past two hundred men and a priest without lighting anything. You taught her that. [short pause] Rook is at the edge of the square with six men, watching. He came to see you lose. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

50a585c7280e9d81.text: Get her out the back before they reach the room. Do not make her test it. [short pause] She goes over the yard wall. The dog goes after her. Halfway down the lane the dog’s tail catches fire, just the tail, just for a second, and the dog goes home. [short pause] They lose her. They also now know exactly what they are looking for, and that it has been taught. The Fire’s eye on you grows.

51637c369a44e2a6.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] Rook has a warrant and thirty men and nothing left to be ashamed of. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, and he will be behind you for years. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

51851c17471dc5c6.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

5228c3d8a010b4bf.text: Do nothing. Trust the hiding place. [short pause] He puts the torch up the flue. Liesl screams. They have her out and in the cage inside a minute, and Pip is a smear of soot on the hearthstone, crying. [short pause] The town watched you stand there. Trust drops.

528395255222a28d.text: The quest board. [short pause] You take the corner table and the room rearranges itself around you. Men stop mid-sentence. Berna the innkeeper brings wine without being asked and a list of everything wrong with her town, in order of what she would pay to have fixed. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "Start anywhere. The well’s the quietest. The bridge is the funniest. Don’t start with the hunters." [long pause] One: Salt in the Well. [short pause] Two: The Toll. [short pause] Three: The Spark. [short pause] Four: Old Wood. [short pause] Five: Long Shadows.

52e6c55dde28d300.text: The spark. [short pause] Captain Tybalt Rook of the Eternal Fire, Redania’s church and its witch-burning police, rides in with six men and a cage on wheels. He is handsome, soft-spoken, and has burned eleven women this year, which he mentions during the sermon the way a farmer mentions rain. [short pause] He is here because a letter said a child in this town sets things on fire when she is frightened. Liesl, the baker’s girl. Twelve. The bread has been coming out black for a month. He says he will be here three days, and that he always finds what he comes for. [short pause] Rook’s eyes slide over you, pause, and move on. Good. The glamour on your face is holding. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "He’s a bad one. I can smell what he had for breakfast and it was a person’s fear." [short pause] The sermon ends with a question to the crowd: does anyone here know the girl? [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Say nothing. Find the baker before Rook does. [short pause] Two: Speak up. "Every child in Velen has burned a loaf. Go home."

52e7f20a9ee92f81.text: Tell her the truth: keep him off the well water, and he will mend. Slowly. [short pause] She believes you, because you did not try to sell her anything. [short pause] Tam will be sick for a week. He will live. Ida will tell the village the stranger said it was the water, not the witch.

52f06357c60932f9.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is alive, and she was in that chimney for all of it. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

53038243f782b653.text: Long shadows. [short pause] Horns on the south road. A Nilfgaardian raiding column, two hundred soldiers of the southern empire, come to burn a river town for the lesson it teaches other river towns. They need the bridge to cross the Pontar. Everyone in Greyhollow needs it more. [short pause] Behind the column, under the Eternal Fire’s banner, is the rest of Rook’s order. Thirty men with torches, here for whoever killed a captain. They have an understanding with the Nilfgaardians: the town is theirs to burn, you are the Fire’s to keep. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: Pip: "Bridge first. Everything else is after." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Light a fire on the north tower first. The elves said they would see it. [short pause] Two: The bridge. Now.

531d8f437dd11c56.text: The knock. [short pause] Nothing comes at midnight. Rook has what he came for, or has decided this town is not worth a fourth day. [short pause] Matthis is in the cage in the square. Rook leaves at first light for Oxenfurt, and the baker is going with him as a lesson. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Break the cage before dawn. Quietly. [short pause] Two: Let him go.

5498c1c5a75e6e46.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in a cage on the Oxenfurt road. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

550293a49acf2409.text: The quest board. [short pause] Pip is not in the chimney. Pip is on the table, which has never happened, and Pip says: "Horns. On the south road. You should finish your drink." [long pause] One: Salt in the Well. [short pause] Two: The Toll. [short pause] Three: The Spark. [short pause] Four: Old Wood. [short pause] Five: Long Shadows.

552e1af4d6aed753.text: Let him have Lukas. The boy is standing right there. [short pause] You step aside. It takes about as long as you would think. [short pause] When it is over the wraith is gone, satisfied, and Lukas is at the bottom of the well with the man he put there. [short pause] Ashbrook saw you step aside. Trust drops hard.

5537af1bc54def7d.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

55422bce048d649c.text: The well. Look before you listen. [short pause] You go down first. Nobody argues.

55466e649faebf01.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest is just trees now. [short pause] The Order wants you more than Nilfgaard wants the town. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, tonight, and not stopping for a while. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

56271a571cb69fd5.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan is a pile of rock at the foot of the arch. Carts roll over him. [short pause] Four elves are in the Mahakam hills, alive, because of you. They told you to light a fire on the north tower when the horns come. [short pause] Nilfgaard thinks there are crossbows on the towers. [short pause] Someone paid the Redanian garrison to leave. You do not know who yet. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

5680a4ca8ebfb924.text: Offer it a different tithe: the guild leaves the wood forever, and Thornwick doubles the bread. [short pause] It takes a long time. Old things do not like new terms. But you stood at the rite, and it saw you do it. [short pause] It accepts. Ysolde’s mark fades. The guild is told, by you, in front of their own graves, that the wood is closed. Aldo leaves Greyhollow rather than say he was beaten by a tree. [short pause] Nobody dies. Thornwick does not know how to thank you. Trust rises.

57282bc893f759c2.text: Kill him anyway. A bridge is a bridge. [short pause] He does not fight back much. He keeps looking at the ledge. [short pause] A hundred crowns. The elves are alone now.

57989462183d8cf6.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is on the bridge, but he does not know you, and he does not know whose side you are on. He fights the first thing that reaches him. It is a Nilfgaardian, which is luck, not loyalty. [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

57ede4be8caaeb5c.text: The crossing. [short pause] The Redanian picket is six bored men and a lantern. The elves need to be past them and into the Mahakam foothills before dawn. [short pause] You could put six men to sleep with one word. Six men would also wake up knowing exactly what put them there. [short pause] The grandfather says he will not make the swim. He says it like a man stating the weather. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Glamour the whole picket. Six men dream of their mothers for an hour. [short pause] Two: Take them across the water, below the picket, the hard way. Carry the old man. [short pause] Three: Bribe the picket. Twenty crowns and the sergeant goes blind for an hour. [short pause] Four: This is too far. Wish them luck.

58004715ba33cb0d.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] L. B. Half the men in Ashbrook have a B in their name. Only one of them has a father with glass windows. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Talk to Marga. [short pause] Two: Talk to Berthold. [short pause] Three: Wait for nightfall at the well.

582f3625fcaf97a8.text: The inn, and the thing in the chimney. [short pause] You ride into Greyhollow at dusk with two swords on your back and rain in your collar. The town is thirty houses and a stone bridge, and every one of the thirty houses watches you pass. The inn is called the Drowned Rat. The sign is a rat. It is, in fact, drowning. [short pause] Berna runs the inn. Sixty, wide, unimpressed by anything that has ever walked through her door. She puts a bowl of stew in front of you and a list on the table: everything wrong with her town, in order of what she would pay to have fixed. "You look like you fix things," she says. It is not a compliment. [short pause] Then something falls down the chimney. [short pause] It is the size of a cat, black with soot, with enormous eyes and a face like a very old child. It dusts itself off, climbs onto the table, looks you up and down, and says: "Right. I’m Pip. I’m a godling. That’s a house spirit, before you ask. I’ve lived in that chimney ninety years. I know everybody in this town by smell. I know who’s lying. I know where the bodies are, and I mean that literally, there are at least four. And you’re going to need me." [short pause] Berna does not look up. "He does this," she says. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "I’m coming with you. I’ll ride in your coat. I’ll be quiet mostly. When I talk, listen, because I’m usually right and I’m always smug about it." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: "Fine. Stay out of the way." [short pause] Two: "I work alone."

585922be239b1daf.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She can light one candle without lighting the others. She stared down the Fire at her own kitchen table. 58869b844ac9e2fd.text: Break the cage before dawn. Quietly. [short pause] One sleeping guard, one Axii, one bent bar. Whoever was in the cage is back in the inn before the chapel bell. [short pause] Rook wakes to an empty cage and knows exactly who did it. He leaves anyway. He has a column to ask for.

5897c4e790c91889.text: Fight through them. [short pause] You let them see you. Properly. The glamour comes off and the room fills with a light that is not fire, and six men learn what the Order has been burning women to avoid. [short pause] Rook dies with his medallion in his fist. The cage opens on its own. Oxenfurt will hear, and the next letter will be a column.

[short pause] Two: Take Hodd’s side. The town first. Point Rook at a stranger on the road.

Bogdan saw the purse." [short pause] So the garrison did not march north. It was bought off. Someone wanted this bridge unguarded.

The Order will never stop.

[short pause] Rook asks to speak with you anyway. Alone, he says, and then brings two men. He is polite. He knows what you are. Against you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. The bakery is three doors from the inn. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Lie. Smoothly. The girl ran off to Oxenfurt a week ago. [short pause] Two: Bribe him. Fifty crowns for a letter that says Greyhollow is clean. [short pause] Three: Let him see your eyes. Remind him what a witcher does to men who threaten him. [short pause] Four: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here?

[short pause] Two: Burn the totems and fight it with the mark intact. Take the mark on yourself. [short pause] Three: Walk away. Tell Aldo the forest is not lumber.

A man asks her name. She tells him the boring story you gave her, in the boring voice. Then Rook comes in, pulls a chair up close, and asks her what her mother’s name was. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Answer for her. "Her mother was Hanna. Died of the flux. Anything else?" [short pause] Two: Let her answer.

[short pause] Berna opens the cage herself. Rook leaves at dawn with it empty and a face like a slapped priest. [short pause] He will not forget this. Trust rises.

[short pause] The sergeant takes the money and turns his back and says, to nobody, "I did not see four elves and I will not see them again." [short pause] Four people owe you. So, in a way, does a Redanian sergeant who now has a secret.

[short pause] Two: Keep the letter. One day it may be worth something to someone. [short pause] Three: Burn it. The dead do not need mail.
