6c5115713a5e048c.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

6d56a72bb47a1a6e.text: Threaten him. Let him see what you are. [short pause] He steps back. He is not stupid. But his eyes go to the edge of the bridge, down, and back to you, and you understand he is not scared for himself.

6d5fc195bdfcb3e2.text: Questions. [short pause] Dren the clerk is in the cage, white as his own candles. Father Ansel is standing beside it with his hands folded, saying nothing, which is the bravest thing he can manage. [short pause] Rook asks to speak with you anyway. Alone, he says, and then brings two men. He is polite. He knows what you are. He asks where the baker’s girl is, and then, before you answer, he asks about Ashbrook, and the bridge, and a light some people saw. [short pause] He is enjoying this. He is looking at your mouth while you talk, and you know that look, and it is not the one men usually give you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. The bakery is three doors from the inn. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Lie. Smoothly. The girl ran off to Oxenfurt a week ago. [short pause] Two: Hex him. Make him forget the girl’s name. [short pause] Three: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here?

6d6026c71214aef7.text: Give her a charm that turns eyes away from her door. [short pause] You twist three of her chicken feathers and a hair of your own into a knot and hang it on the lintel. Nobody will find this hut tonight unless they already know the way. [short pause] Someone in the square saw the light in your hands. The Eternal Fire’s eye on you grows.

6d8fcca63231673a.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is alive because a ninety-year-old chimney spirit threw every pot in the kitchen. She and Pip are inseparable now. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

6da378764721bf67.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

6e1d7bbf72c7b8ed.text: Long shadows. [short pause] Horns on the south road. A Nilfgaardian raiding column, two hundred soldiers of the southern empire, come to burn a river town for the lesson it teaches other river towns. They need the bridge to cross the Pontar. Everyone in Greyhollow needs it more. [short pause] You know who paid the Redanian garrison to leave now. It was this. Someone in Nilfgaard bought an empty bridge a month ago and is coming to collect. [short pause] Rook is with them, at the back, with a face that has been waiting for this. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: Pip: "Bridge first. Everything else is after." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Light a fire on the north tower first. The elves said they would see it. [short pause] Two: The bridge. Now.

6e7ceb2f7688d6ad.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

6e86bb4147bbae1e.text: Speak up. "Every child in Velen has burned a loaf. Go home." [short pause] The square laughs. Rook does not. He writes something in a small book without looking down at it. [short pause] Greyhollow likes you for it. So does Rook, in the way a cat likes a mouse that moved.

6f38ad9817e2d3b1.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Ashbrook with Marga and the chickens, learning things nobody writes down. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

6fb8186de9672efc.text: Questions. [short pause] Rook asks to speak with you anyway. Alone, he says, and then brings two men. He is polite. He knows what you are. He asks where the baker’s girl is, and then, before you answer, he asks about Ashbrook, and the bridge, and a light some people saw. [short pause] He is enjoying this. He is looking at your mouth while you talk, and you know that look, and it is not the one men usually give you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. The bakery is three doors from the inn. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Lie. Smoothly. The girl ran off to Oxenfurt a week ago. [short pause] Two: Bribe him. Fifty crowns for a letter that says Greyhollow is clean. [short pause] Three: Hex him. Make him forget the girl’s name. [short pause] Four: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here?

70a1e0072a2bc6d3.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

70b885b317080746.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

72538d9b9fca1912.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

72a4137d91753178.text: Old wood, closed. [short pause] The north wood tonight: [short pause] The leshen is dead and its mark is in you. [short pause] A forest remembers who kept faith with it, and who did not.

72e61566351c5c2c.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

73c643b900a350c2.text: Three days. [short pause] Rook has three days and six men. They will search every house. Matthis asks what you can do. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hide her in the inn chimney. Pip will keep her company. [short pause] Two: Teach her to lie. Axii for the nerves, and a story she can hold. [short pause] Three: Send her to Auntie Yew in Nettle Fen. The hag will take a child like this.

73d1c88f4ba6b157.text: Let them take Matthis. She is safe where she is. [short pause] The street watches a baker go into a cage for a daughter who is miles away. Nobody says your name. Nobody has to. [short pause] Trust drops hard. Liesl will hear about this wherever she is.

742ff32f4fef7003.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] The Order built a pyre in the square before the raid was even over. Liesl is on it, and the torches are lit, and thirty men in white are between you and her. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. Rook. He has a warrant and a column and nothing left to be ashamed of. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The pyre. Cut her down, whatever it costs. [short pause] Two: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Three: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

7466b4b0c6d20017.text: The spark. [short pause] Captain Tybalt Rook of the Eternal Fire, Redania’s church and its witch-burning police, rides in with six men and a cage on wheels. He is handsome, soft-spoken, and has burned eleven women this year, which he mentions during the sermon the way a farmer mentions rain. [short pause] He is here because a letter said a child in this town sets things on fire when she is frightened. Liesl, the baker’s girl. Twelve. The bread has been coming out black for a month. He says he will be here three days, and that he always finds what he comes for. [short pause] Rook’s eyes find you in the crowd and stay there. He is not looking at a woman. He is looking at a pyre with a woman in front of it. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "He’s a bad one. I can smell what he had for breakfast and it was a person’s fear." [short pause] The sermon ends with a question to the crowd: does anyone here know the girl? [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Say nothing. Find the baker before Rook does. [short pause] Two: Speak up. "Every child in Velen has burned a loaf. Go home."

74b39f710853956c.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] A letter is going south to a woman named Livia. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

74c3214a58c6d4bc.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

750658d4c8fe5e63.text: The square. [short pause] Greyhollow is burning. The inn, the chapel, the mill. There are Nilfgaardians in the square and they are not in a hurry. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

7592476fb83cb16b.text: Guests and trespassers. [short pause] The forest speaks to you before you are a hundred yards in. Not words. Pressure. A door opening in your chest. It knows what you are and it is pleased, the way a king is pleased when another king visits. [short pause] The red cloth on your arm is doing something. The wolves keep their distance. The crows watch and do not call. [short pause] Ahead, at a fork in the path, is a totem taller than the others, hung with a fresh deer skull. The path to the left goes to Thornwick’s side of the wood. The path to the right goes deeper, toward where the trees stop making sense. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Burn the big totem. See what the wood does. [short pause] Two: Leave it. Walk the left path, toward Thornwick. [short pause] Three: Walk the right path. Straight at it.

75aa4ff78890e3e9.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest is just trees now. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

75c30a9d7d6107a0.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

768849f6729d3cc6.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

76d2bf1c332e5d4c.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] Liesl is in the chimney with Pip. Liesl was in the chimney for all of it. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. A new captain. He has Rook’s medallion on a cord around his wrist. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

76e66833032101ab.text: Lay him to rest. Give him his name, burn the knife, let the boy say it. [short pause] You cannot do a rite. But a killer can. Lukas stands at the well and says the name three times into the water, and you hold the knife in a fire until the handle goes. [short pause] He turns south. He goes. The well is only a well. [short pause] The village saw it. Trust rises.

76f2755cbdf44220.text: What is down there. [short pause] You go down on a rope with a torch in your teeth. Thirty feet down, the water is black and cold and your medallion is humming hard enough to hurt. [short pause] There is a body under the water. A soldier in Nilfgaardian black, throat cut, a millstone roped to his chest. He has been there about a month. A letter in his coat, half rotted: his name is Aurelio, he deserted at the Pontar crossing, and he was walking home to a town called Vicovaro to see his mother before she died. [short pause] His killer left the knife in him. A hunting knife, good steel, with two letters burned into the handle. L. B. [short pause] And he is not a drowner, the common river monster the village assumes. He is becoming a wraith: a ghost made from a bad death, angry, and tied to the place it died. In a day or two he will be done becoming. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take the letter and the knife. [short pause] Two: Leave him as he is. Touch nothing.

76f5f7ac11300a7b.text: Salt in the well. [short pause] Ashbrook is an hour upriver: thirty houses, a mill, a shrine to whichever god was listening last, and one well. The well tastes of iron. Two cows are dead, a child is sick, and the village has decided this is the work of the widow Marga, who sells herbs and talks to her chickens. [short pause] Berthold, the ealdorman (the village headman, the closest thing Ashbrook has to a mayor), has sent to Greyhollow for help. Sixty crowns to "deal with whatever is down there." [short pause] You have been that old woman, in other villages, under other names. You feel the mood of a square the way other people feel weather. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "Ashbrook. Good bread, bad gossip. The miller’s wife cheats at dice. I’ll be quiet now." [short pause] On the road in, a woman is running toward you with a boy in her arms. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Stop. Look at the boy. [short pause] Two: Keep walking. The well first, then the sick.

77c97a594e1b4687.text: Send her to Marga in Ashbrook. An old woman with chickens is the last place anyone looks. [short pause] Matthis drives her out before dawn in a cart of flour sacks. [short pause] Marga meets them at the gate, takes one look at the girl, and says "Oh, you’re one of mine." Nobody knows what she means by it.

77fac5a769f4ea34.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan is a pile of rock at the foot of the arch. Carts roll over him. [short pause] Four elves are in the Mahakam hills, alive, because of you. They told you to light a fire on the north tower when the horns come. [short pause] Three Nilfgaardian scouts did not come home. [short pause] Someone paid the Redanian garrison to leave. You do not know who yet. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

78306177b5bf77ee.text: The search. [short pause] Four of Rook’s men come through the inn at dusk with torches and a dog. They are not subtle. They turn over the beds, they open the flour barrels, they put a boot through Berna’s cellar door. [short pause] Father Ansel is with them, as the town’s priest, and Father Ansel is being extraordinarily slow. He has lost his keys. He has found his keys. He needs to bless the cellar before anyone enters it. Nobody can tell if he is a coward or a hero and he seems unsure himself. [short pause] Liesl is in the back room, sitting at the table with her hands folded. A man asks her name. She tells him the boring story you gave her, in the boring voice. Then Rook comes in, pulls a chair up close, and asks her what her mother’s name was. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Answer for her. "Her mother was Hanna. Died of the flux. Anything else?" [short pause] Two: Let her answer.

78c886985bc0da0f.text: Tell the sergeant there will be more, and the rate is the same. [short pause] He nods. A Redanian sergeant who takes elf money is a Redanian sergeant who will not look too hard at anything else either. [short pause] You have bought a hole in the north bank. It may be useful.

7905bea81ed63e41.text: Who wrote the letter. [short pause] Rook came because of a letter. Someone in Greyhollow wrote to Oxenfurt about a baker’s girl. Matthis has been thinking about nothing else for a month. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "I know who. The chapel clerk. Father Ansel’s clerk, Dren. He smells like wax and spite. Ansel didn’t know. Ansel’s soft." [short pause] Father Ansel is the town’s priest of the Eternal Fire. Soft, Pip says. Dren is the one who keeps his books. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Go see Father Ansel. If he is soft, he is useful. [short pause] Two: Go see Dren. Find out why. [short pause] Three: It does not matter who. Deal with the girl.

799d04ec9b87a9e3.text: "Fine. Stay out of the way." [short pause] Pip climbs into your coat pocket like it was built for him. It smells of soot for the rest of the story.

79a6c337d20b0ad4.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is alive, and she was in that chimney for all of it. [short pause] Dren the clerk went to Oxenfurt in her place. The Fire ate its own, and Father Ansel has not slept since. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

79e147daad03f682.text: Cut a White Honey draught ten to one with river water and make him drink it. [short pause] He vomits black for a full minute. Then he breathes. Then he asks for bread. [short pause] Ida does not say thank you. She says "Who else?" and you understand she means the well. [short pause] Ashbrook will remember this. Trust rises.

7a1b6bc33468c822.text: Marga, before the rope gets used. [short pause] You reach her hut as two men with the rope are deciding whether to knock. [short pause] They see you and remember urgent business elsewhere.

7a53727e5479547e.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] Dren the clerk went to Oxenfurt in her place. The Fire ate its own, and Father Ansel has not slept since. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

7ad105f61699c17d.text: Wait for nightfall at the well. [short pause] You sit with your back to the stone and wait for the thing to finish becoming.

7bb97353f1b2acd2.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is on the bridge, but he does not know you, and he does not know whose side you are on. He fights the first thing that reaches him. It is a Nilfgaardian, which is luck, not loyalty. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

7bbce01a03036a0b.text: Fight. End it clean. [short pause] You bind him in a circle of light bright enough to be seen from the chapel, and you unmake him with a word your teachers told you never to use in public. [short pause] It worked. Half the village saw the light. The Fire’s eye on you grows.

7c2fb108e3192414.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] Liesl is in Ashbrook with Marga. Nothing came near Ashbrook. A charm on a lintel, maybe. Marga is not saying. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. Rook. He has a warrant and a column and nothing left to be ashamed of. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

7cbb7bd020084f8f.text: The price. [short pause] Aldo wants it dead. Thornwick wants it fed. Ysolde wants to be sixteen. The leshen wants what it has always wanted, and will take it from someone. [short pause] There is no clean door. Pick one. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Kill Ysolde. Then the leshen. It is the only clean way. [short pause] Two: Burn the totems and fight it with the mark intact. Take the mark on yourself. [short pause] Three: Bargain with it. Offer it better prey than a village girl: the ones in white, when they come back. [short pause] Four: Offer it a different tithe: the guild leaves the wood forever, and Thornwick doubles the bread. [short pause] Five: Walk away. Tell Aldo the forest is not lumber.

7d15d96f702d8ca2.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio went home. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

7d3c44d4625ebb78.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

7dc8ac6cbd45ebe5.text: Aurelio. [short pause] He comes up out of the well like smoke that forgot it was supposed to rise. Black coat, open throat, a face that is still mostly a face. He speaks Nilfgaardian, then Common, then just sound. He is asking which way is south. He is asking for his mother. [short pause] You know his name. That matters more than silver. [short pause] Silver out. Yrden ready. You could end this in a minute. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Fight. End it clean. [short pause] Two: Lay him to rest. Give him his name, burn the knife, let the boy say it. [short pause] Three: Axii. Point him at the river and let him walk.

7e3f621688bab2d6.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

7e42dcd67b085a74.text: The knock. [short pause] They come at midnight. Rook and all six, torches, the cage on wheels, a warrant he wrote himself. Someone told him where you sleep. Pip says the alderman did, and Pip is usually right about who smells of guilt. [short pause] They are not here for Liesl first. They are here for you. [short pause] You know something they do not: Oxenfurt never sent him. Whatever happens tonight, there is no one behind him. Yet. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Fight through them. [short pause] Two: Run. Out the back, into the dark. [short pause] Three: Walk out the front door and make him explain, to the whole street, why six armed men need a cage for a baker’s child.

7e9a49ef6d1dda6e.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam is mending. [short pause] A letter is going south to a woman named Livia. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

7eefcb63ceaf1262.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. [short pause] Rook is at the edge of the square with six men, watching. He came to see you lose. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

7f188cd9fa3f4fc3.text: Keep your distance. You have seen refugees before. [short pause] You stay on the steps. The children watch you the whole time.

802be2a9ee7ab333.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. A new captain. He has Rook’s medallion on a cord around his wrist. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

8131d722d24dca59.text: Pay in a story. Tell him something true about yourself. [short pause] You tell him about the night Aretuza found out what you could really do, and what it cost the girl in the next bed. [short pause] He is quiet a long time. Then he says you can cross for free forever, and asks if you want to see what is under the bridge.

8144ed945f9785b7.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio went home. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

822dc14def6341c9.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Look at the well. [short pause] Two: Talk to Berthold. [short pause] Three: Go up to the hunting blind. Find Lukas before dark. [short pause] Four: Wait for nightfall at the well.

827fe01811524f5d.text: Take the purse. Say nothing yet. [short pause] Eleven florens. Nilfgaardian silver. He watches you pocket it and does not ask. [short pause] Now he thinks you can be paid. That may be useful.

82b1d2c4c009ff30.text: Stop them. Nobody takes the baker. [short pause] You do not touch anyone. You say "Let him go," and the irons open on their own, and every man on the street sees them open. [short pause] The street cheers. Rook, from the chapel steps, writes it down.

82e64726066b67e2.text: The world in one page. [short pause] You do not need to know the Witcher books or games to play this. Here is everything that matters. [short pause] The war. Two big powers are fighting over this part of the world. Nilfgaard is the empire from the south: black armor, disciplined, winning. Redania is the northern kingdom: paranoid, run by a king who burns anyone who can do magic. Greyhollow is a small river town stuck on the line between them. The river is the Pontar. The one stone bridge over it is the only reason anyone cares about the town. [short pause] The Eternal Fire. Redania’s state church. Its witch hunters ride around in white cloaks arresting and burning sorceresses, mages, and anyone who looks like one. They answer to the city of Oxenfurt. In this game they are the people a sorceress is hiding from. [short pause] Witchers. Men taken as boys and changed with mutations so they can hunt monsters for money. Cat eyes, two swords (steel for people, silver for monsters), and five simple spells called Signs: Aard (a shove), Igni (fire), Quen (a shield), Yrden (a trap), and Axii (a calming mind-trick). Most people fear them a little and hire them anyway. A medallion around their neck hums near magic. [short pause] Sorceresses. Trained at a school called Aretuza. Powerful, long-lived, beautiful by choice (they fix their own faces with magic), and political. The Lodge was their secret club of the most powerful ones. A glamour is a spell that changes how you look. [short pause] Monsters you will meet. A wraith is a ghost that formed from a bad death. A botchling or lubberkin is what a dead unnamed baby can become. A troll is big, slow, talks, and is not evil. A leshen is an ancient forest spirit shaped like a stag-headed tree; it protects its woods and demands a tithe. A godling is a tiny, friendly, chatty nature spirit. A hag is an old swamp witch who takes children. A pesta is a plague ghost. [short pause] Elves. The Aen Seidhe are the elves who lived here before humans. Humans pushed them into the hills and now hunt the ones who fight back, who are called Scoia’tael. In Redania an elf caught near a road is usually hanged. [short pause] Words. Ealdorman or alderman means village headman. A pellar is a village healer and spirit-talker. Crowns are money. Velen is the poor, swampy province the town sits in. Mahakam is the dwarf mountain country to the east where runaways go. [short pause] That is it. The rest you will pick up as you go. Pip will explain things when it matters. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Back to where I was.

83209a955cc17ef2.text: Take Aldo’s coin and go in. [short pause] A hundred and twenty crowns, half now. Aldo says the forest is lumber. He says it like a man who has never been in it at night.

839870472b5f39d2.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

84087507bb7f3037.text: The marked one. [short pause] You find the mark on a tree by Thornwick’s well: a name cut in Elder runes. Ysolde. Hesper’s granddaughter. Sixteen. [short pause] The bead Wat gave you is hers. She was at the oak the night it fell. She was there to stop them. [short pause] She is at the well, drawing water, and she has known for a week. She asks you not to tell her grandmother. "Gran will try to give herself instead. The wood won’t take her. It wants someone who still has years." [short pause] A marked one is the leshen’s tithe. While she lives, the forest is fed and quiet. If you kill the marked one, the leshen loses its anchor and can be destroyed. If the leshen is destroyed with the mark intact, the mark passes to whoever killed it. [short pause] She knows all of that too. She has had a week. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Promise her you will not tell Hesper. [short pause] Two: Tell her you make no promises until you have seen the thing. [short pause] Three: Tell her the truth: the cleanest way out of this is her.

84ecb56e6fb13807.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

85c882196d292aa9.text: The search. [short pause] Four of Rook’s men come through the inn at dusk with torches and a dog. They are not subtle. They turn over the beds, they open the flour barrels, they put a boot through Berna’s cellar door. [short pause] One of them stops at the hearth and looks up. The dog is looking up too. Pip is up there with Liesl, and Pip is a nature spirit, not a soldier. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let Pip handle it. Godlings are good at being somewhere else. [short pause] Two: Axii the man at the hearth. He has seen nothing. [short pause] Three: Do nothing. Trust the hiding place.

86054b02cc7b5add.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

86a2be4437eb2abb.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

86b32e7ab4176748.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is on the bridge, but he does not know you, and he does not know whose side you are on. He fights the first thing that reaches him. It is a Nilfgaardian, which is luck, not loyalty. [short pause] Lukas and eleven Ashbrook bows come down the river road at a run. He finds you on the bridge and says "You said someday." [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

86d93c9144e9315d.text: Stop. Look at the boy. [short pause] His name is Tam. He is six. His lips are grey and his breathing is wrong, and his mother, Ida, has been carrying him since dawn because the village told her the witch did it and she does not know what else to do.

870d933035206334.text: Ask her to stand up and say it in the square. [short pause] She is quiet a long time. "If you are standing next to me. Not behind. Next to." [short pause] You agree. Trust rises; she has decided you are worth something.

8740f418fd6fe4b6.text: Old wood. [short pause] Two petitions reach the inn the same morning. Aldo, foreman of the woodcutters’ guild, will pay a hundred and twenty crowns for the leshen in the north wood: three men dead, the rest refusing to go in. A leshen is an ancient forest spirit, antlered and tree-tall, that commands the wolves and crows and treats the wood as its own. Elder Hesper of Thornwick, the village at the wood’s edge that still keeps the old gods, will pay nothing and asks you, please, to leave the forest its master. [short pause] The leshen has marked someone. Thornwick will not say who. The woodcutters do not care who. [short pause] Leshens are not killed, they are unmade. Totems first, then the thing itself, and even then they come back if the wood wants them to. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take Aldo’s coin and go in. [short pause] Two: Go in for Thornwick. See what the forest wants.

8796a45f753ad8c0.text: The square. [short pause] Half the town is burning. The chapel. The mill. Not the inn. Pip’s chimney is the only chimney on that street still up, and there are Nilfgaardians in the square. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. Rook. He has a warrant and a column and nothing left to be ashamed of. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Face the Order here. Say the thing out loud: nobody sent them. [short pause] Two: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Three: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

87b3153e1b0de4fb.text: The boy. [short pause] The whole village is in the square at dawn, because Berthold’s son confessed in his father’s kitchen last night and the maid heard it through the floor. Lukas is standing by the well with his hands at his sides. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope.

87b91c632103225c.text: Questions. [short pause] The tinker is in the cage. He is shouting that he has never done magic in his life, which is true, and which Rook has heard before. [short pause] Rook asks to speak with you anyway. Alone, he says, and then brings two men. He is polite. He knows what you are. He asks where the baker’s girl is, and then, before you answer, he asks about Ashbrook, and the bridge, and a light some people saw. [short pause] He is enjoying this. He is looking at your mouth while you talk, and you know that look, and it is not the one men usually give you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. The bakery is three doors from the inn. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Lie. Smoothly. The girl ran off to Oxenfurt a week ago. [short pause] Two: Bribe him. Fifty crowns for a letter that says Greyhollow is clean. [short pause] Three: Hex him. Make him forget the girl’s name. [short pause] Four: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here?

8874ce5f035120db.text: Riders in black. [short pause] On the way to the bridge you meet three Nilfgaardian scouts coming the other way: black cloaks, good horses, maps. They are counting. Bridges, fords, how many men a town could put on a wall. They are polite, the way an army is polite before it arrives. [short pause] Their sergeant asks you, as a traveler, whether the Greyhollow bridge is held. [short pause] He is looking at you the way men look at you, and then a second time the way soldiers look at a map. He has seen sorceresses at court. He is trying to decide if you are one. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Tell him the truth. A troll holds it, and the town has no garrison. [short pause] Two: Lie. "A Redanian company. Crossbows on both towers." [short pause] Three: Kill them. Quietly. Three men fall off three horses and the horses go home alone.

888bc4433ef57a11.text: Lie. "A Redanian company. Crossbows on both towers." [short pause] He looks at you a long moment. Then writes it down anyway. [short pause] It will cost whoever comes up this road an extra day of caution. A day can matter.

89a2a9e7cea0e8dc.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas hangs from the mill. His father will not speak your name. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

8a394d139608ddbd.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

8acc71551227985d.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

8b30f422f29b3a11.text: Old wood, closed. [short pause] The north wood tonight: [short pause] The leshen is fed. Aldo is the meal. [short pause] A forest remembers who kept faith with it, and who did not.

8bb033492f45ed04.text: The leshen. [short pause] It comes at midnight, after the rite, because you are at the treeline alone and it has been curious since the road. Antlers like a fallen tree. A body that is bark and shadow and crows. It does not have a face. It has a place where a face would be, and the place looks at you. [short pause] It speaks to you as an equal, because tonight you are. Old power recognizes old power. It asks, without words, what you want. [short pause] It tells you the terms, which have not changed in a thousand years. One life, freely marked, and the wood keeps the peace. The oak was cut. The price went up. Three woodcutters were the interest. Ysolde is the principal. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Ask it to take the debt out of the guild instead. They cut the oak. [short pause] Two: Ask it what it fears. [short pause] Three: Say nothing. Let it finish, and decide.

8bdca9bab9e6373c.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] In front of the bakery, a twelve-year-old girl is standing very still with her hands folded. A Nilfgaardian captain, or what is left of one, is on the cobbles in front of her. She lit one candle, and only one, and it was him. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

8c27cdeed7394ed7.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

8c5230ad39d58bca.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

8cb8576fb9593be3.text: Take them across the water, below the picket, the hard way. Carry the old man. [short pause] Cold enough to stop a heart. The grandfather’s nearly does. You carry him the last hundred yards on your back. [short pause] Nobody saw. Four people owe you.

8d0eac7713d1fb99.text: The thing the grandfather said. [short pause] At the treeline the grandfather stops and takes your hand again. He says, in the old Common: "You will need us. Not soon. But you will. When the horns come, light a fire on the north tower and we will see it." [short pause] Then they are gone into the hills, and it is just you and the river and Pip, who is pretending not to have cried. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Go home. Light a fire on the tower someday.

8d5ff3a17e68071c.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. Her father is in a cage on the Oxenfurt road. The fen will hear about that. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

8de6c16eda64f40d.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas hangs from the mill. His father will not speak your name. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

8e70f973b42b530c.text: The narrow part. [short pause] It holds. Against all sense, it holds, because everyone you ever did right by is standing on it with you. The column is bunched on the south ramp, taking arrows, and the men at the front have started looking behind them. [short pause] There is a thing you could do here. One word, the real one, the one Aretuza took girls to the cellar for saying. It would end this. It would be seen from Oxenfurt, from Novigrad, from the moon. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Say the word. [short pause] Two: Hold with what you have. No more than that.

8eefebb2911a726d.text: Old wood, closed. [short pause] The north wood tonight: [short pause] The leshen is dead. Ysolde is dead. The wolves are gone. [short pause] A forest remembers who kept faith with it, and who did not.

8f2affee827082e5.text: Take Jens’s twenty on the side as well. Nobody needs to know. [short pause] Twenty crowns from a man who wants the opposite of what you were just paid to do. Pip says "Oh, that’s not going to stay secret." [short pause] It does not. Trust drops.

8f436051e081924a.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas got away with it, and the village burned an old woman’s house for your silence. [short pause] Marga is gone. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

900866a166193e88.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in a cage on the Oxenfurt road. [short pause] Dren the clerk went to Oxenfurt in her place. The Fire ate its own, and Father Ansel has not slept since. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

90208e15f31d0ac4.text: The quest board. [short pause] Berna wipes the table. Pip rustles in your pocket. The board has more on it than it did. [long pause] One: Salt in the Well. [short pause] Two: The Toll. [short pause] Three: The Spark. [short pause] Four: Old Wood. [short pause] Five: Long Shadows.

9052978cd2ca3e12.text: The boy. [short pause] Lukas is waiting for you at the gate with a hunting bow across his knees, which tells you he knows. He says the soldier was stealing their winter seed. He says he only meant to scare him. He says it twice. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [short pause] Ida is in the crowd with Tam on her hip. She is watching you, not Lukas. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope.

908a5a31c6f2750c.text: The inn, and the thing in the chimney. [short pause] You ride into Greyhollow at dusk, and the town, which has been grey for three hundred years, notices. Men stop mid-sentence. A woman at a well forgets the bucket. You are used to it. You put a little more into the glamour anyway, out of habit, and the glamour takes it. The inn is called the Drowned Rat. The sign is a rat. It is, in fact, drowning. [short pause] Berna runs the inn. Sixty, wide, unimpressed by anything that has ever walked through her door. She puts a bowl of stew in front of you and a list on the table: everything wrong with her town, in order of what she would pay to have fixed. "You look like you fix things," she says. It is not a compliment. [short pause] Then something falls down the chimney. [short pause] It is the size of a cat, black with soot, with enormous eyes and a face like a very old child. It dusts itself off, climbs onto the table, looks you up and down, and says: "Right. I’m Pip. I’m a godling. That’s a house spirit, before you ask. I’ve lived in that chimney ninety years. I know everybody in this town by smell. I know who’s lying. I know where the bodies are, and I mean that literally, there are at least four. And you’re going to need me." [short pause] Berna does not look up. "He does this," she says. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "I’m coming with you. I’ll ride in your coat. I’ll be quiet mostly. When I talk, listen, because I’m usually right and I’m always smug about it." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: "Fine. Stay out of the way." [short pause] Two: "I do not travel with pets."

90b53a8f9a33ade1.text: Bribe him. Fifty crowns for a letter that says Greyhollow is clean. [short pause] He takes it without looking at it. "The Fire is grateful for your donation." [short pause] He does not call off the search. He just stops looking at you while it happens. The eye on you softens, slightly.

90eebf069e0f38a0.text: Tam. [short pause] You put your hand on his chest and feel it: not a curse. Rot. Something dead in the water, and its slow black breath in his lungs. You could burn it out of him. It would cost you, and someone on this road would see. [short pause] Ida is watching your hands. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Burn it out of him. Here. Now. [short pause] Two: Tell her the truth: keep him off the well water, and he will mend. Slowly.

90f34d0d99d447cd.text: Guests and trespassers. [short pause] Wolves first. They do not attack. They walk beside you, three on each side, like an escort, or a guard. Your medallion has not stopped humming since the treeline. The totems are everywhere: antlers, bone, red string. [short pause] The red cloth on your arm is doing something. The wolves keep their distance. The crows watch and do not call. [short pause] Ahead, at a fork in the path, is a totem taller than the others, hung with a fresh deer skull. The path to the left goes to Thornwick’s side of the wood. The path to the right goes deeper, toward where the trees stop making sense. [long pause] What do you do? 928ca7008d32edb7.text: The world in one page. [short pause] You do not need to know the Witcher books or games to play this. Here is everything that matters. [short pause] The war. Two big powers are fighting over this part of the world. Nilfgaard is the empire from the south: black armor, disciplined, winning. Redania is the northern kingdom: paranoid, run by a king who burns anyone who can do magic. Greyhollow is a small river town stuck on the line between them. The river is the Pontar. The one stone bridge over it is the only reason anyone cares about the town. [short pause] The Eternal Fire. Redania’s state church. Its witch hunters ride around in white cloaks arresting and burning sorceresses, mages, and anyone who looks like one. They answer to the city of Oxenfurt. In this game they are the people a sorceress is hiding from. [short pause] Witchers. Men taken as boys and changed with mutations so they can hunt monsters for money. Cat eyes, two swords (steel for people, silver for monsters), and five simple spells called Signs: Aard (a shove), Igni (fire), Quen (a shield), Yrden (a trap), and Axii (a calming mind-trick). Most people fear them a little and hire them anyway. A medallion around their neck hums near magic. [short pause] Sorceresses. Trained at a school called Aretuza. Powerful, long-lived, beautiful by choice (they fix their own faces with magic), and political. The Lodge was their secret club of the most powerful ones. A glamour is a spell that changes how you look. [short pause] Monsters you will meet. A wraith is a ghost that formed from a bad death. A botchling or lubberkin is what a dead unnamed baby can become. A troll is big, slow, talks, and is not evil. A leshen is an ancient forest spirit shaped like a stag-headed tree; it protects its woods and demands a tithe. A godling is a tiny, friendly, chatty nature spirit. A hag is an old swamp witch who takes children. A pesta is a plague ghost. [short pause] Elves. The Aen Seidhe are the elves who lived here before humans. Humans pushed them into the hills and now hunt the ones who fight back, who are called Scoia’tael. In Redania an elf caught near a road is usually hanged. [short pause] Words. Ealdorman or alderman means village headman. A pellar is a village healer and spirit-talker. Crowns are money. Velen is the poor, swampy province the town sits in. Mahakam is the dwarf mountain country to the east where runaways go. [short pause] That is it. The rest you will pick up as you go. Pip will explain things when it matters. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Got it. Who am I playing?

b0b13eee577792a4.text: The boy. [short pause] Lukas is waiting for you at the gate with a hunting bow across his knees, which tells you he knows. He says the soldier was stealing their winter seed. He says he only meant to scare him. He says it twice. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope.

b103216772b01735.text: Glamour. Show him the river and call it the road home. [short pause] He believes you. He walks into the Pontar and under it, still asking for his mother. [short pause] The well is clean. The river is not. Something is in it now that remembers you.

b1124582a765fa9d.text: "I am what they call a witch. Look at me. Do I look like a monster to you?" [short pause] She looks at you the way girls look at you, which is to say: like you are the answer to a question she had not finished asking. "No," she says. "You look like a queen."

b1271f5d4d4eaa24.text: Fight through them. [short pause] Six men with torches against a witcher in a doorway. It is not a fight, it is a lesson. Rook dies last, on the steps, surprised. [short pause] You break the cage open with a pommel. Oxenfurt will hear a captain of the Order died in Greyhollow, and the next letter will be a column.

b149e8dc451f1f92.text: Leave him as he is. Touch nothing. [short pause] You come back up with nothing but the name. The knife stays in him. [short pause] Without the knife there is no proof. Without the letter there is no address.

b189607a4795103a.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] In front of the bakery, a twelve-year-old girl is standing very still with her hands folded. A Nilfgaardian captain, or what is left of one, is on the cobbles in front of her. She lit one candle, and only one, and it was him. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

b1d258b20f17f97b.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

b250fd8fe4204da9.text: Talk to Marga. [short pause] Her chickens are loose in the lane. Someone got here before you.

b27cb3665fc9ed0c.text: The pyre. Cut her down, whatever it costs. [short pause] You do not go through them. You stand at the edge of the square and the pyre goes out. All of it, at once, cold, as if it had never been lit. Thirty men turn around. [short pause] You walk through them to the stake and untie her yourself. Nobody moves. She is alive. The Order will never stop.

[short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

[short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

b3bacb66100546ce.text: Riders in black. [short pause] On the way to the bridge you meet three Nilfgaardian scouts coming the other way: black cloaks, good horses, maps. They are counting. Bridges, fords, how many men a town could put on a wall. They are polite, the way an army is polite before it arrives. [short pause] Their sergeant asks you, as a traveler, whether the Greyhollow bridge is held. [short pause] He is looking at your swords. He knows what they mean. Witchers are neutral, as far as empires are concerned, and empires are never quite sure. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Tell him the truth. A troll holds it, and the town has no garrison. [short pause] Two: Lie. "A Redanian company. Crossbows on both towers." [short pause] Three: Kill them. Three fewer maps in Nilfgaard.

b3c061bf671c3153.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] At the head of the column, under the black banner, a captain reins in and shouts a name across the bridge. "Aurelio." Then: "Who wrote to Vicovaro?" [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Answer the captain. "I did. He was laid to rest. His mother knows." [short pause] Two: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Three: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

b438a495274559a5.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran from the bridge into the north wood did not come out of the north wood. Thornwick left bread at your door again. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

b43d860bce78cfb7.text: The afternoon. [short pause] You have seen the well, the widow, and the man with the glass windows. The sun is low. [short pause] You have a name and a knife that match. Lukas. L. B. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Go up to the hunting blind. Find Lukas before dark. [short pause] Two: Wait for nightfall at the well.

b45a126cbd840df4.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Ashbrook with Marga and the chickens, learning things nobody writes down. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

[long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The pyre. Cut her down, whatever it costs. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

b5b17a539bcddf35.text: Kill Ysolde. Then the leshen. It is the only clean way. [short pause] You do it fast, at the well, and she does not see you coming. [short pause] The forest screams through every tree at once. The leshen dies two hours later, anchorless, on its knees. The wolves leave. The totems rot by morning. [short pause] Aldo pays the rest. Thornwick will never speak to you again, and Greyhollow heard what you did. Trust collapses.

b5bc805f89e8b560.text: Bogdan. [short pause] Bogdan is nine feet of river rock with moss for eyebrows and a toll-collector’s satchel that used to be a Redanian saddlebag. He stands in the middle of the bridge with his arms folded and says: "Toll. Cheese or story. No story about a dog. Bogdan has heard every dog story." [short pause] Your medallion barely stirs. Rock trolls are not monsters, whatever the council thinks. They are just very large and very bad at negotiating. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Pay in a story. Tell him something true about yourself. [short pause] Two: Pay in a story. Make one up. [short pause] Three: Fight. The council wants a bridge. [short pause] Four: Threaten him. Trolls understand a witcher.

b6423852809e45df.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran from the bridge into the north wood did not come out of the north wood. Thornwick left bread at your door again. [short pause] Rook has a warrant and thirty men and your real face in his memory. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, and he will be behind you for years. He has found his purpose, and it is you. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

b686d8e0a7886343.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] Dren the clerk went to Oxenfurt in her place. The Fire ate its own, and Father Ansel has not slept since. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

[short pause] Four elves went north in Redanian irons. The chapel thinks well of you. [short pause] Nilfgaard thinks there are crossbows on the towers. [short pause] Someone paid the Redanian garrison to leave. You do not know who yet. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

[short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

His father will not speak your name. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is mending. [short pause] A letter is going south to a woman named Livia. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

b7247290117bf6f8.text: The square. [short pause] Greyhollow is burning. The inn, the chapel, the mill. There are Nilfgaardians in the square and they are not in a hurry. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. A new captain. He has Rook’s medallion on a cord around his wrist. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

b72aa77f1c797b66.text: The widow. [short pause] Marga is seventy and furious and not at all surprised to see you. She knows exactly what is in the well. She saw Lukas, the ealdorman’s son, at the well one night a month ago, with a rope, with something heavy, with the look of a boy who has just found out what he is. [short pause] She has told nobody. "Who would I tell? Him?" She means Berthold. [short pause] She looks at your eyes for a long moment. "Cat eyes. My grandmother said your kind can tell a lie from a truth by the smell. Can you?" You can, a little. She is not lying. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Promise to keep her name out of it. [short pause] Two: Ask her to stand up and say it in the square.

[short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

They turn over the beds, they open the flour barrels, they put a boot through Berna’s cellar door. [short pause] Father Ansel is with them, as the town’s priest, and Father Ansel is being extraordinarily slow. He has lost his keys. He has found his keys. He needs to bless the cellar before anyone enters it. Nobody can tell if he is a coward or a hero and he seems unsure himself. [short pause] She is not here and they know it. So they take Matthis instead. Two men walk the baker out of his own shop in irons. "Bait," Rook says, pleasantly, to the street. "Children come home for their fathers." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let them take Matthis. She is safe where she is. [short pause] Two: Stop them. Nobody takes the baker.

c0317bad66aceaa3.text: The old faith. [short pause] Thornwick keeps the rite at the new moon: the whole village at the edge of the wood with lanterns and bread and a goat, singing something older than Common. Hesper leads it. She does not know the name on the tree. She knows there is a name. [short pause] They leave the bread and the goat at the treeline. The wood takes them. It does this every month, and has for longer than the village has had a name, and in return the wood does not take anything else. [short pause] Hesper asks you to stand with them. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Stand with them. Sing if you can. [short pause] Two: Watch from outside the circle. [short pause] Three: Tell Hesper the name on the tree.

c0ae105e8c9a40cd.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She can light one candle without lighting the others. She stared down the Fire at her own kitchen table. She looks at you like you hung the moon. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Four: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

c1dc477e2ffce885.text: Who walks into Greyhollow? [short pause] Greyhollow is a river town on the Pontar, right on the line between two armies. Nilfgaard, the empire, holds the south bank. Redania, the kingdom, holds the north. Witch hunters from Oxenfurt ride through whenever the chapel sends a letter. The town sits on its one stone bridge and hopes nobody important notices it. [short pause] Somebody important is about to. [long pause] One: Garrick of Ard Carraigh, the witcher. [short pause] Two: Ilvara of Aretuza, the sorceress.

c1f019f0b3c5c41c.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest did not stop them. The forest was busy with you. The coal behind your sternum is awake tonight, and something with antlers is walking beside you that nobody else can see. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

c2098937f0dfd8ac.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. He is looking at your mouth while you talk, and you know that look, and it is not the one men usually give you. [short pause] Behind him, his men are already going door to door. [short pause] Ida does not say thank you. She says "Who else?" and you understand she means the well. [short pause] Ashbrook will remember this. Trust rises. So does the chance someone on the road describes the light to the wrong person.

Berthold hangs his own son from the mill beam because no one else will, and then sits under him until noon. [short pause] Ashbrook trusts you now. Ashbrook also has no one left who can draw a bow. [short pause] Marga stood next to you and said it. You stood next to her.

[short pause] Two: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Three: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

He charges a toll: a wheel of cheese, or a story he has not heard. Carts will not pay in cheese, merchants will not pay in stories, and the ferryman, Jens, has started charging what a man charges when he is the only ferry. [short pause] The council is five people shouting. Alderman Hodd wants the bridge cleared and offers a hundred crowns. Jens, at the back, offers twenty more for it to stay exactly as it is. The grain merchants want a bridge and do not care who stands on it. Old Berna from the inn wants to know why nobody has simply asked the troll what he wants. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: "Bogdan’s all right. It’s the cheese that’s the problem. Nobody in this town can make cheese." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take Hodd’s contract. A hundred crowns for a clear bridge. [short pause] Two: Take Jens’s twenty on the side as well. Nobody needs to know. [short pause] Three: Ask Berna’s question. What does the troll actually want?

cb915560cb0bc2d6.text: Let her answer. [short pause] "Hanna," Liesl says, and the candle on the table goes up like a torch. [short pause] Rook smiles for the first time since he rode in. The cage door closes. Trust drops.

cccc97603f805b4f.text: The narrow part. [short pause] It holds for an hour. Then the right-hand parapet goes and they are over it in a wave, and you are backing up the bridge one yard at a time. [short pause] There is a thing you could do here. One word, the real one, the one Aretuza took girls to the cellar for saying. It would end this. It would be seen from Oxenfurt, from Novigrad, from the moon. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Say the word. [short pause] Two: Hold with what you have. No more than that.

[short pause] Four: Blame the drowner. Take the money. Leave.

[short pause] One: Cut a White Honey draught ten to one with river water and make him drink it. [short pause] Two: Tell her the truth: keep him off the well water, and he will mend. Slowly.

d08c81787ad0964a.text: Help them cross north tonight. [short pause] You will need the Redanian picket to look the other way.

[short pause] Two: Lay him to rest. Give him his name, burn the knife, let the boy say it. [short pause] Three: Glamour. Show him the river and call it the road home.
