Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

e6afdb1e2e728bae.text: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch. [short pause] Bogdan will not come off it. "Bogdan is the toll." The arch goes into the Pontar with him on it, and two hundred men on the wrong side of the water. [short pause] No bridge. No raid. Greyhollow is an island now, and Jens the ferryman is the richest man in it.

e6e58ce54b9047b0.text: Teach her to lie. Axii for the nerves, and a story she can hold. [short pause] You cannot teach her magic. You can teach her to be boring. A calm face, a dull story, and a little Axii so her hands do not shake. [short pause] It will hold for one interrogation. Maybe.

e7a5f9422c5f6897.text: Long shadows. [short pause] Horns on the south road. A Nilfgaardian raiding column, two hundred soldiers of the southern empire, come to burn a river town for the lesson it teaches other river towns. They need the bridge to cross the Pontar. Everyone in Greyhollow needs it more. [short pause] You know who paid the Redanian garrison to leave now. It was this. Someone in Nilfgaard bought an empty bridge a month ago and is coming to collect. [short pause] Pip, from your pocket: Pip: "Bridge first. Everything else is after." [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Light a fire on the north tower first. The elves said they would see it. [short pause] Two: The bridge. Now.

e8587cd87d294f8d.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] At the head of the column, under the black banner, a captain reins in and shouts a name across the bridge. "Aurelio." Then: "Who wrote to Vicovaro?" [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Answer the captain. "I did. He was laid to rest. His mother knows." [short pause] Two: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Three: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

e8a9aa1490fed395.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] A letter is going south to a woman named Livia. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

e8d28a3c2e493796.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

e8f21b1fad33358c.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

e9376a01b4ef9276.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is alive because a ninety-year-old chimney spirit threw every pot in the kitchen. She and Pip are inseparable now. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

e9b70224ce16be70.text: Tell Hodd about the elves. The council pays for that too. [short pause] Hodd pays sixty crowns and sends a rider to the Redanian picket. The elves are gone by morning. You do not ask where. [short pause] The chapel notes that you are loyal. The Fire’s eye on you softens. [short pause] Pip climbs out of your pocket and walks home.

e9d6cd836f0e46c0.text: Promise to keep her name out of it. [short pause] She nods once. "Then you carry it."

ea316a3be7eab092.text: Bogdan. [short pause] Bogdan is nine feet of river rock with moss for eyebrows and a toll-collector’s satchel that used to be a Redanian saddlebag. He stands in the middle of the bridge with his arms folded and says: "Toll. Cheese or story. No story about a dog. Bogdan has heard every dog story." [short pause] Your medallion barely stirs. Rock trolls are not monsters, whatever the council thinks. They are just very large and very bad at negotiating. [short pause] Berna’s cheese is under your arm. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Pay in cheese. [short pause] Two: Pay in a story. Tell him something true about yourself. [short pause] Three: Pay in a story. Make one up. [short pause] Four: Fight. The council wants a bridge. [short pause] Five: Threaten him. Trolls understand a witcher.

eae9868d138dadea.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She can lie with a straight face now. Rook has her mother’s name in his book. [short pause] Rook: alive, humiliated in front of a whole street, and writing a very long letter. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

eb46f14d81fad2b9.text: What is down there. [short pause] You do not go down. You prick your thumb, let one drop fall into the bucket, and the well tells you itself, in the back of your skull, like a man shouting underwater. [short pause] There is a body under the water. A soldier in Nilfgaardian black, throat cut, a millstone roped to his chest. He has been there about a month. A letter in his coat, half rotted: his name is Aurelio, he deserted at the Pontar crossing, and he was walking home to a town called Vicovaro to see his mother before she died. [short pause] His killer left the knife in him. A hunting knife, good steel, with two letters burned into the handle. L. B. [short pause] And he is not a drowner, the common river monster the village assumes. He is becoming a wraith: a ghost made from a bad death, angry, and tied to the place it died. In a day or two he will be done becoming. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take the letter and the knife. [short pause] Two: Leave him as he is. Touch nothing.

ebd5abb775c3452a.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan stands on it in a hat, taking two crowns a cart and telling everyone the dragon story. [short pause] Four elves are in the Mahakam hills, alive, because of you. They told you to light a fire on the north tower when the horns come. [short pause] Three Nilfgaardian scouts did not come home. [short pause] Someone paid the Redanian garrison to leave. You do not know who yet. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

ec0a236a9a69189d.text: Break the cage before dawn. Quietly. [short pause] One sleeping guard, one whispered word, one lock that decides it was never a lock. Whoever was in the cage is back in the inn before the chapel bell. [short pause] Rook wakes to an empty cage and knows exactly who did it. He leaves anyway. He has a column to ask for.

ec74d1e11e94db4a.text: The square. [short pause] The column is going back down the south road. The square is full of people who did not expect to be alive and are not sure what to do with it. [short pause] Auntie Yew walked out of Nettle Fen at midnight with Liesl beside her, and whatever Liesl is now, it has a voice like a well and eyes like the bottom of one. Liesl does not look at you once. She knows who let them take her father. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

ecac82246f80b11c.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

ed36647939dd64c1.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is gone, which is not the same as home. [short pause] Lukas is on the north road with a bow. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam is mending. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

edb5e221524fdfcf.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in a cage on the Oxenfurt road. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

ee4add955c68d6f7.text: Promise her you will not tell Hesper. [short pause] She breathes out. "Thank you." She goes back to drawing water, because the goats still need it, marked or not.

ee84050cfae07d78.text: Stop them. Nobody takes the baker. [short pause] You take the irons off him with your hands. The two men decide they have other errands. [short pause] The street cheers. Rook, from the chapel steps, writes it down.

efbbc4b55c8ba0c4.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio went home. [short pause] Lukas hangs from the mill. His father will not speak your name. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

eff1af3da8c162a8.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Ashbrook with Marga and the chickens, learning things nobody writes down. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

f08ceb402e3795fd.text: Glamour the whole picket. Six men dream of their mothers for an hour. [short pause] Six men sit down in the road and smile at nothing. The grandfather kisses your hand. The children do not look back. [short pause] Somewhere in the hills, four people owe you. Six men will wake up and remember a woman walking past them in a light that was not the lantern. The Fire’s eye on you grows.

f15fdbe5542c6de2.text: Berthold. [short pause] Berthold is a big man gone soft, with a son he talks about too much and a wife he does not mention. He says the well has a drowner in it, obviously, and the old woman called it, obviously, and he would be grateful if you dealt with both and did not make a parade of it. [short pause] He slides a purse across the table. Eighty crowns. Twenty more than the contract. "For discretion." [short pause] He is sweating the way men sweat when they think a woman has not noticed something. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Take the purse. Say nothing. [short pause] Two: Leave it on the table. [short pause] Three: Ask him where Lukas was a month ago.

f1f662e7edb720ee.text: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Village law is old and short. Berthold hangs his own son from the mill beam because no one else will, and then sits under him until noon. [short pause] Ashbrook trusts you now. Ashbrook also has no one left who can draw a bow.

f245dc6f8fc663ef.text: Walk out the front door and make him explain, to the whole street, why six armed men need a cage for a baker’s child. [short pause] It works because the town is already outside, holding lanterns, and because Rook, for all his sermons, has never once been asked a question by a crowd. [short pause] You ask the question that matters: "Who sent you?" He has no answer the street will accept. [short pause] Berna opens the cage herself. Rook leaves at dawn with it empty and a face like a slapped priest. [short pause] Liesl climbs down from the chimney covered in soot and bows. The town laughs. Rook hears it from the road. [short pause] He will not forget this. Trust rises.

f2fb10051802fea4.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

f3c66987878421e8.text: The price. [short pause] Aldo wants it dead. Thornwick wants it fed. Ysolde wants to be sixteen. The leshen wants what it has always wanted, and will take it from someone. [short pause] There is no clean door. Pick one. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Kill Ysolde. Then the leshen. It is the only clean way. [short pause] Two: Burn the totems and fight it with the mark intact. Take the mark on yourself. [short pause] Three: Give it Aldo. He cut the oak. [short pause] Four: Bargain with it. Offer it better prey than a village girl: the ones in white, when they come back. [short pause] Five: Offer it a different tithe: the guild leaves the wood forever, and Thornwick doubles the bread. [short pause] Six: Walk away. Tell Aldo the forest is not lumber.

f4b823c55b80696b.text: Ask it to take the debt out of the guild instead. They cut the oak. [short pause] It considers. It would accept the one who ordered the cutting. It names him without a name: the one with the red face and the boots. [short pause] Aldo. It will take Aldo, and release the girl.

f4d3a6516f783d09.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] The bridge is empty. The pile of rock at the foot of the arch does not help anyone. [short pause] A few arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. Elven arrows. Four people owed you, and they are doing what four people can. [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Something comes up out of the Pontar under the arch. Black coat, open throat. It takes the first rank of Nilfgaardians into the water by the ankles, and it keeps looking at you. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

f5ffb59bd2dffac3.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is alive, and she was in that chimney for all of it. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] You know Rook came on his own, not on orders. That is a thing to say out loud, in front of the right people, on the right night. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: elsewhere, for now. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

f657cb68fc71fac8.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Look at the well. [short pause] Two: Wait for nightfall at the well.

f6e7578c3219eacd.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran from the bridge into the north wood did not come out of the north wood. Thornwick left bread at your door again. [short pause] The Order wants you more than Nilfgaard wants the town. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, tonight, and not stopping for a while. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

f73a4859eeac8708.text: The leshen. [short pause] It comes at midnight, after the rite, because you are at the treeline alone and it has been curious since the road. Antlers like a fallen tree. A body that is bark and shadow and crows. It does not have a face. It has a place where a face would be, and the place looks at you. [short pause] Leshens do not speak. This one does, in the way the oldest ones can, straight into the part of your head the Trials opened. It knows what you are. It has met your kind before. It did not enjoy it. [short pause] It knows you burned the totem. It is not angry. It is interested, the way a cat is interested in a mouse that bit it. [short pause] It tells you the terms, which have not changed in a thousand years. One life, freely marked, and the wood keeps the peace. The oak was cut. The price went up. Three woodcutters were the interest. Ysolde is the principal. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Ask it to take the debt out of the guild instead. They cut the oak. [short pause] Two: Ask it what it fears. [short pause] Three: Say nothing. Let it finish, and decide.

f7a8676dfb80caf9.text: Write to Livia. Tell her where her son is, and that he was laid to rest. [short pause] Ten crowns to the merchant. You write it plainly. You do not say who killed him. [short pause] Somewhere in Nilfgaard a woman will get a letter from a stranger in Velen. Nilfgaard is large, and the army is larger, and letters travel in strange directions.

f7be7aa6d66938ca.text: Three days. [short pause] Rook has three days and six men. They will search every house. Matthis asks what you can do. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hide her in the inn chimney. Pip will keep her company. [short pause] Two: Teach her. Tonight. Control, not fear. [short pause] Three: Send her to Auntie Yew in Nettle Fen. The hag will take a child like this.

f89e94186fb5536e.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio took what he was owed. [short pause] Lukas is in the well. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam is mending. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

f8a03efca3f66602.text: The square. [short pause] Half the town is burning. The chapel. The mill. Not the inn. Pip’s chimney is the only chimney on that street still up, and there are Nilfgaardians in the square. [short pause] Liesl kept her face dull and her story boring and walked past two hundred men and a priest without lighting anything. You taught her that. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

f8b266d776149deb.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] Liesl is in Ashbrook with Marga. Nothing came near Ashbrook. A charm on a lintel, maybe. Marga is not saying. [short pause] Rook is at the edge of the square with six men, watching. He came to see you lose. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

f9075852f8afdb3a.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is on the bridge, but he does not know you, and he does not know whose side you are on. He fights the first thing that reaches him. It is a Nilfgaardian, which is luck, not loyalty. [short pause] Behind them, Ida, with Tam left at home and a pitchfork in both hands, and twenty more from Ashbrook who remember a stranger on a road. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

f946696ca4f16265.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio took what he was owed. [short pause] Lukas is in the well. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

f954b9cf51e96792.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is the bravest person in Ashbrook, and they know it now. [short pause] Tam is alive and eating. Ida tells everyone who will listen. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

f9568eeedc0d54b1.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest is just trees now. [short pause] Rook came to watch you lose. He watched the opposite. He leaves on the same road he came in on, and he has nothing to write to Oxenfurt about. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

fa18f1b699fa3976.text: The toll, closed. [short pause] The bridge tonight: [short pause] Bogdan stands on it in a hat, taking two crowns a cart and telling everyone the dragon story. [short pause] Four elves went north in Redanian irons. The chapel thinks well of you. [short pause] Nilfgaard thinks there are crossbows on the towers. [short pause] A bridge is the kind of thing that matters most on the one night it matters.

fa59dd94b6a81c9f.text: Aurelio. [short pause] He comes up out of the well like smoke that forgot it was supposed to rise. Black coat, open throat, a face that is still mostly a face. He speaks Nilfgaardian, then Common, then just sound. He is asking which way is south. He is asking for his mother. [short pause] You never went down. You do not know his name, and he can tell. [short pause] Silver out. Yrden ready. You could end this in a minute. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Fight. End it clean. [short pause] Two: Lay him to rest. (You need his name, his letter, and someone who can say it: Marga unshaken, or Lukas willing.) [short pause] Three: Axii. Point him at the river and let him walk.

fa61b80e917747d9.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest is just trees now. [short pause] Rook has a warrant and thirty men and your real face in his memory. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, and he will be behind you for years. He has found his purpose, and it is you. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

fa8c0dff308ae472.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Arrows come out of the dark on the north bank. A lot of arrows. Elven arrows, from the Mahakam side. Four people owed you. They brought everyone. [short pause] The column comes up the road slow, in cover, expecting crossbows on the towers. It costs them twenty minutes they did not have. [short pause] Two hundred men. You could do something about two hundred men. It would be seen from Oxenfurt. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Drop the arch into the river.

fad94b8b884d4d35.text: Guests and trespassers. [short pause] Wolves first. They do not attack. They walk beside you, three on each side, like an escort, or a guard. Your medallion has not stopped humming since the treeline. The totems are everywhere: antlers, bone, red string. [short pause] You came in on Aldo’s coin, with no cloth on your arm, and the wood knows it. The wolves are closer than you would like. [short pause] Ahead, at a fork in the path, is a totem taller than the others, hung with a fresh deer skull. The path to the left goes to Thornwick’s side of the wood. The path to the right goes deeper, toward where the trees stop making sense. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Igni the big totem. See what the wood does. [short pause] Two: Leave it. Walk the left path, toward Thornwick. [short pause] Three: Walk the right path. Straight at it.

faf5a428f24cfdec.text: What runs into the trees. [short pause] What ran into the north wood regrouped there and came back at dusk. The forest did not stop them. The forest was busy with you. The coal behind your sternum is awake tonight, and something with antlers is walking beside you that nobody else can see. [short pause] The Order wants you more than Nilfgaard wants the town. You will be leaving Greyhollow by the north road, tonight, and not stopping for a while. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: The ledger.

fb641d7341302b41.text: The afternoon. [short pause] The sun is dropping. Whatever is in the well will be done becoming by dark. [short pause] Lukas himself has not been seen all day. His mother says he is at the hunting blind on the ridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Look at the well. [short pause] Two: Talk to Marga.

fb6fca7f9b14d4f4.text: Answer the captain. "I did. He was laid to rest. His mother knows." [short pause] Silence on the bridge for the length of a breath. The captain is Aurelio’s brother. He got the letter in a field camp three weeks ago and has not slept properly since. [short pause] He does not call off the column. He cannot. But he pulls his own company, forty men, off the bridge and onto the south bank, and tells them to watch the road. Forty fewer. He looks at you once more and does not look again. [short pause] You hold the bridge with what is left.

fbdc2177d439b71b.text: The alderman’s offer. [short pause] Hodd sends for you after dark. He has a bottle open and the shutters closed. He is a practical man. He has done the arithmetic: a witch hunter who leaves happy is cheaper than a witch hunter who leaves angry. [short pause] "I don’t care about the girl," he says. "I care about the town. Give him something. Give him the girl, give him the old woman in Ashbrook, give him a stranger off the road. He goes home, we go back to work." [short pause] He likes you. You handed him the elves. He thinks you understand how things work. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: "Give him nothing. He leaves with an empty cage or he leaves with a problem." [short pause] Two: "Give him Dren. The clerk wrote the letter. Let the Fire eat its own." [short pause] Three: Take Hodd’s side. The town first. Point Rook at a stranger on the road.

fc08d639b429e536.text: Hold or burn. [short pause] Bogdan is already on the bridge, hat on, satchel off, a Redanian cart-axle in each hand. "Toll," he says to two hundred men, "is a story. Bogdan has not heard this one." [short pause] Ashbrook sends nobody with a bow. Ashbrook has nobody to send. [short pause] Silver is wrong for this. Steel, then, and Quen, and the narrowest part of the bridge. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Hold the bridge. Make them pay for every yard. [short pause] Two: Fire the bridge. Igni on the old timbers under the arch.

fc1d04b547d47a73.text: Go see Dren. Find out why. [short pause] Dren is twenty-five and owes the bakery money. That is the whole reason. A debt, a letter, a child in a cage. [short pause] You do not hit him. You let him understand that you thought about it. [short pause] He will not be writing any more letters. He may also tell Rook you threatened him.

fc1ef973b62a5fb8.text: Hide her in the inn chimney. Pip will keep her company. [short pause] Pip is delighted. "I’ve never had a guest." Liesl climbs up with a blanket and a loaf of bread. [short pause] It is a good hiding place. It is only a hiding place, and Rook has three days.

fc25c7652033195c.text: Salt in the well, closed. [short pause] What you leave behind in Ashbrook: [short pause] Aurelio is in the river. [short pause] Lukas lives, and owes you. [short pause] Marga is alive and keeps her chickens. [short pause] Tam lived, barely. Ida tells everyone who will listen that you walked past. [short pause] Some of this comes back.

fd54f7c804a74afc.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Ashbrook with Marga and the chickens, learning things nobody writes down. [short pause] Rook: dead on the inn steps. Oxenfurt will send more. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: watching. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

fd766b12eb90c305.text: The boy. [short pause] The whole village is in the square at dawn, because Berthold’s son confessed in his father’s kitchen last night and the maid heard it through the floor. Lukas is standing by the well with his hands at his sides. [short pause] His father is on the porch behind him, not coming down the steps. [short pause] Ida is in the crowd with Tam on her hip. She is watching you, not Lukas. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Name him in the square. Let the village judge. [short pause] Two: Deal with him privately. He owes you now. [short pause] Three: Make him Ashbrook’s problem. Exile, not a rope.

fdcd49dac1c7e49f.text: The square. [short pause] The town stands because the bridge does not. Nilfgaard will be back in the spring with boats. That is spring’s problem. [short pause] Liesl is in the chimney with Pip. Liesl was in the chimney for all of it. [short pause] And in the middle of the square, with thirty white cloaks behind him, is the Order. A new captain. He has Rook’s medallion on a cord around his wrist. [long pause] What do you do? [short pause] One: Let the Order come. You have other things to do tonight. [short pause] Two: Into the north wood, after what is running there.

fdfb44fd670346a9.text: Leave it. Walk the left path, toward Thornwick. [short pause] The wolves peel off at the edge of the village fields. One of them looks back at you, which wolves do not do.

fe9843fdafe107a8.text: Lay him to rest. Give him his name, burn the knife, let the boy say it. [short pause] You say his name into the water three times and burn the knife in your bare hand, which hurts exactly as much as it should. [short pause] He turns south. He goes. The well is only a well. [short pause] Nobody saw a light, because there was none. The village saw you cry a little, which did you more good than a spell.

ff1b2b7166c79b82.text: Answer every question with a question. Where is his warrant? Who signed it? Does Oxenfurt know he is here? [short pause] He has a warrant. It is signed by himself. Oxenfurt does not, in fact, know he is here; he came on a clerk’s letter, not an order. [short pause] You have learned something. He has learned you noticed.

ff564a34392eb2e2.text: Go see Dren. Find out why. [short pause] Dren is twenty-five and owes the bakery money. That is the whole reason. A debt, a letter, a child in a cage. [short pause] You do not hex him. You let him see you decide not to. [short pause] He will not be writing any more letters. He may also tell Rook you threatened him.

ff7eeaeca304d4e5.text: The spark, closed. [short pause] Liesl: [short pause] She is in Nettle Fen. Pip will not say her name anymore. [short pause] A tinker with no name went to Oxenfurt in her place. The town knows whose idea that was. [short pause] Rook: alive, and your name is in his book. [short pause] The Fire’s eye on you: wide open. [short pause] What this changes later: who stands in the square on the night the horns sound, and whether thirty white cloaks come back for you.

ffc892aa27f0da7c.text: "Give him Dren. The clerk wrote the letter. Let the Fire eat its own." [short pause] Hodd thinks about it for exactly as long as it takes to pour another drink. "The clerk. Yes. The clerk has always been a problem." [short pause] Rook will have a name by morning. It will not be Liesl’s. It will not be yours. Pip says "Huh," in a tone you cannot read.

ffd3d1de21df1728.text: Say nothing. Let it finish, and decide. [short pause] It finishes. It waits. The wood waits with it.
